claim_hierarchy.claim: Near-complete Ross aggregate recovery was produced by strongly unequal local restoration and did not completely restore pre-disturbance spatial composition at either six-component or three-colony grain.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: State-restoration magnitude is spatial-grain dependent; the qualitative path-versus-state discrepancy is robust.

claim_hierarchy.claim: High inverse-path fidelity co-occurred with weak or negative state restoration in all three complete Ross down-up episodes at six-component grain.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: The three episodes are not independent replicates.

claim_hierarchy.claim: Persistent decline at Palmer and Signy reweighted breeding structure beyond proportional thinning.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Specific vital-rate mechanisms are not identified.

claim_hierarchy.claim: Beaufort growth after capacity release reweighted breeding structure beyond proportional expansion while independent inter-island export declined.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Census and movement evidence are independent streams, not mediation.

claim_hierarchy.claim: Unequal local recovery can produce apparently complete aggregate recovery while changing spatial dominance and redundancy; apparent state restoration depends on observation grain.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: No universal scale-free state-restoration index is claimed.

main_sentence: Near-complete aggregate recovery was produced by differential local recovery: the population recovered where it had declined, but not in the same proportions, and the degree of apparent state restoration depended on spatial grain.
withdrawn_claims: Ross restored or re-expressed the pre-shock spatial state
high inverse-path fidelity implies state restoration
state restoration equals 2.4% as a scale-invariant property
near-complete aggregate recovery means most breeding components nearly recovered
the focal result demonstrates latent spatial memory
